knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)

# them but doesn't run them again.
knitr::opts_hooks$set(engine = function(options) {
  if (options$engine == "bash") options$eval <- FALSE
  options
})

<!--
Explain what this step does and why, and copy each command you ran into a
bash chunk. R chunks run from the top of the repository.
-->

```{steps: metabolic_pathways}
# 1. Change directory to [minpath] folder
```{bash}
cd ~/bbd-metagenome/minpath

# 2. Display the prokka.tsv file
```{bash}
# Display .tsv for a single bin
head ../prokka/metabat.48/metabat.48.tsv
# Only show gene ID (column 1) and EC number (column 5)
head ../prokka/metabat.48/metabat.48.tsv | awk -F '\t' '{print $1,$5}'
# Filter output to only include lines with an EC number
head ../prokka/metabat.48/metabat.48.tsv | awk -F '\t' '$5{print $1,$5}'
# Ensure output is tab separated and remove header line
head ../prokka/metabat.48/metabat.48.tsv | awk -F '\t' '$5{OFS="\t";print $1,$5}' | grep -v '^locus'

# 3. Change <head> to <cat> to ensure all genes are being shown
```{bash}
cat ../prokka/metabat.48/metabat.48.tsv | awk -F '\t' '$5{OFS="\t";print $1,$5}' | grep -v '^locus'
# Send output to a file to be used in minpath
cat ../prokka/metabat.48/metabat.48.tsv | awk -F '\t' '$5{OFS="\t";print $1,$5}' | grep -v '^locus' > metabat.48.ec

# 4. Run minpath
```{bash}
minpath -ec metabat.48.ec -report metabat.48.ec.report -details metabat.48.ec.details

# 5. Look at first few lines of output
```{bash}
head metabat.48.ec.report 

# 6. Notes on first line shown: 
path PWY-7321 any n/a  naive 1  minpath 0  fam0  4  fam-found  1  name  ecdysteroid metabolism (arthropods)

# PWY-7321: pathway identifier, which can be used to identify the full pathway
# naive 1: displays that there is one gene from this pathway that was found
# minpath 1: determined that minpath kept this pathway in its minimal set of pathways. If >minpath 0< is displayed, then there is weak evidence for the gene
# fam0 4: determines the amount of gene pathways that are involved in the pathway (four)
# fam-found 2: determines the found gene families from the pathway genome (two out of four)
# name ecdysteroid metabolism (arthropods): name for the pathway

# 7. Use <cat> and <minpath> to get outputs from every bin
```{bash}
# <cat> function
while read bin;do 
  cat ../prokka/$bin/${bin}.tsv | awk -F '\t' '$5{printf("%s\t%s\n", $1,$5)}' | grep -v '^locus' > ${bin}.ec 
done < ../checkm/bbd_topbins.txt
# <minpath> function
while read bin;do 
  minpath -ec ${bin}.ec -report ${bin}.ec.report -details ${bin}.ec.details
done < ../checkm/bbd_topbins.txt

# 8. Find PWY-101 pathway (photosynthesis light reactions) and PWY-5360 pathway (superpathway of tetrathionate reduction)
```{bash}
grep 'PWY-101' *.ec.report
grep 'PWY-5360' *.ec.report

#### Question 4.1 ####
## 1. How many bins contain at least one gene from this pathway?
# Four bins
## 2. Which bin has all of the genes (ie a complete pathway)?
# metabat.30: fam0 4 / fam-found 4
## 3. For which bins does minpath keep the pathway (minpath 1)?
# metabat.10 and metabat.30 both contain minpath 1

#### Question 4.2 ####
## 1. How many bind contain the pathway PWY-5360?
# One bin contains PWY-5360
## 2. What order (in a taxonomic sense) do these bins belong to? Are they in the same family?
# The taxonomic order of this bin is >Campylobacterales<
## 3. How strong is the evidence that these bins really have this pathway? Look at >fam-found< and >minpath< columns
# The evidence for this bin is not very strong, due to the >fam-found< value being 1-out-of-3 and the >minpath< value being 0, meaning other pathways would better explain this gene

# 9. Cross reference results with output from gtdbtk (taxonomy)
```{bash}
grep 'metabat.XX' ../gtdbtk/gtdbtk.bac120.summary.tsv

```

Metabolic pathways inferred from the Prokka annotations with MinPath. Commands for this step were run in `minpath/`.
